items.name: FTP data
items.use: Data channel for active FTP. Port 21 carries commands; knowing FTP is enough on reverse questions.

items.name: FTP control
items.use: Command and control channel for FTP. Port 20 is the active-mode data channel.

items.name: SSH
items.use: Encrypted remote administration; SFTP and SCP can run over SSH.

items.name: SFTP
items.use: Encrypted file transfer carried by SSH; it is not FTP with TLS.

items.name: Telnet
items.use: Unencrypted remote terminal access; SSH is the secure replacement.

items.name: SMTP
items.use: Transfers email between mail servers.

items.name: TACACS+
items.full_name: Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus
items.use: Cisco-associated authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA) protocol.

items.name: DNS
items.use: Name resolution normally uses UDP; TCP is also used, including for larger responses and zone transfers.

items.name: DHCP server
items.use: The DHCP server listens on UDP 67; clients use UDP 68.

items.name: DHCP client
items.use: The DHCP client uses UDP 68; servers listen on UDP 67.

items.name: TFTP
items.use: Simple unauthenticated file transfer, often used for device boot or configuration.

items.name: HTTP
items.use: Unencrypted web traffic.

items.name: Kerberos
items.use: Ticket-based network authentication over TCP or UDP.

items.name: POP3
items.use: Downloads email from a mail server; POP3S uses TCP 995.

items.name: NTP
items.use: Synchronizes clocks across a network.

items.name: SMB over NetBIOS
items.use: Legacy SMB session traffic over NetBIOS; kept as optional reference, not in normal drills.

items.name: IMAP
items.use: Synchronizes email while messages remain on the server; IMAPS uses TCP 993.

items.name: SNMP query
items.use: Management queries and agent responses use UDP 161; traps use UDP 162.

items.name: SNMP trap
items.use: Unsolicited device alerts (traps) are sent to a manager on UDP 162.

items.name: LDAP
items.use: Directory queries and updates; LDAPS uses TCP 636.

items.name: HTTPS
items.use: HTTP protected by TLS.

items.name: SSTP
items.use: VPN tunneling over TLS on TCP 443.

items.name: SMB
items.use: Direct SMB for Windows file and printer sharing.

items.name: ISAKMP / IKE
items.full_name: Internet Security Association and Key Management Protocol
items.use: Negotiates IPsec security associations and key management.

items.name: SMTP submission
items.use: Client mail submission, commonly upgraded to TLS with STARTTLS.

items.name: LDAPS
items.use: LDAP directory traffic protected by TLS.

items.name: FTPS data
items.use: Implicit FTPS data channel; kept as optional reference, not in normal drills.

items.name: FTPS control
items.use: Implicit FTPS control channel; kept as optional reference, not in normal drills.

items.name: IMAPS
items.use: IMAP protected by TLS.

items.name: POP3S
items.use: POP3 protected by TLS.

items.name: RADIUS
items.use: Network authentication and authorization; accounting commonly uses UDP 1813.

items.name: RADIUS accounting
items.full_name: Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service accounting
items.use: RADIUS accounting; kept as optional detail, not in normal drills.

items.name: L2TP
items.use: VPN tunneling protocol that relies on IPsec for encryption.

items.name: PPTP
items.use: Deprecated VPN control channel on TCP 1723; tunneled data uses GRE rather than UDP.

items.name: RDP
items.use: Microsoft remote desktop access.

items.name: Diameter
items.use: AAA successor to RADIUS; kept as optional reference, not in normal drills.

items.name: SRTP
items.use: SRTP normally uses dynamically negotiated media ports; 5004 is not treated as a core fixed port.

items.name: TCP
items.clue: Connection-oriented transport with acknowledgements and retransmission
items.use: Reliable, connection-oriented delivery.

items.name: UDP
items.use: Low-overhead delivery without acknowledgements or retransmission.
